For example, by integrating automated lab reporting that catches missing patient demographics or mismatched diagnostic codes, a health department can precisely track the exact demographics of a localized outbreak without relying on guesswork or delayed follow-up calls.

elements.name: Strengthened population health research and preparedness.
Digitally strengthen public health surveillance and response systems, adverse event reporting, and maximize appropriate secondary use of data for public health purposes.
elements.documentation:
An overarching, comprehensive strategic goal focused on modernizing a nation's health infrastructure through interconnected digital tools, secure data governance, and automated reporting pathways.

Its primary purpose is to transform fragmented health data into a unified, proactive defense network that protects population health by drastically reducing outbreak response times, ensuring medical product safety, and driving evidence-based health policies.

Example: By integrating interoperability gateways, real-time alerting services, and anonymized research databases into a singular national framework, health authorities can instantly detect a localized pathogen spike, monitor any adverse reactions to the deployed treatments, and seamlessly share aggregated data with scientists to refine long-term preventative care.

elements.name: Faster outbreak detection and reduced public health risk.
elements.documentation:
Faster Outbreak Detection and Reduced Public Health Risk is a proactive public health strategy achieved through the integration of real-time digital surveillance and automated diagnostic tracking.

Its primary purpose is to shrink the critical window between the initial emergence of a pathogen and the implementation of control measures, thereby preventing localized clusters from exploding into widespread epidemics.

Example: By linking hospital emergency room data directly to a centralized surveillance network, health officials can detect a sudden, anomalous spike in foodborne illness within hours, allowing them to pull contaminated produce from grocery store shelves before hundreds more people are exposed.

elements.name: Ensure all health workers receive timely payments by adopting reliable digital payroll systems. This includes maintaining a health workforce registry to ensure qualification, retention, capacity building, and career development.
elements.documentation:
The strategic objective focused on implementing robust digital payment infrastructures paired with a dynamic master registry to guarantee prompt compensation and structured professional support for the entire healthcare workforce.

The purpose of this goal is to eliminate payroll delays, minimize administrative discrepancies, and leverage workforce data to boost staff retention, plan targeted training, and secure sustainable career paths for health workers.

Example: "The successful adoption of this comprehensive registry and payroll goal ensured that remote, rural health workers received their monthly salaries and hazard pay directly to their mobile wallets on time, while simultaneously tracking their eligibility for upcoming senior promotions."

elements.name: Implement task-sharing and digital decision support systems to improve the continuity and quality of patient care across healthcare facilities over time to achieve integrated, person-centred care.
elements.documentation:
The strategic objective focused on distributing clinical tasks among multidisciplinary health teams and integrating point-of-care digital guidelines to deliver seamless, longitudinal, and holistic patient care.

The purpose of this goal is to optimize the utilization of the available healthcare workforce, reduce clinical errors, and ensure that individuals receive consistent, high-quality treatment regardless of which facility or practitioner they visit over time.

Example: "The successful execution of the 'Integrated, Person-Centred Care' goal allowed community health workers to utilize mobile digital decision support apps to safely manage and track stable hypertension patients, freeing up specialized physicians to handle complex cases."

elements.name: Patient-level feedback mechanisms integrated into quality reports
elements.documentation:
This outcome collects and integrates patient experiences, satisfaction data, and outcome feedback into healthcare quality reporting processes. It provides insights into care quality from the patient perspective.

The purpose is to strengthen patient-centered care and improve the responsiveness of healthcare services. They also support continuous quality improvement based on patient experiences and outcomes.

Example: Patient satisfaction survey results are included in hospital quality performance reports reviewed by management teams.
